findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock, causing redundant serialized rebuilds
findings.body: GetWebAssets uses a check-lock pattern without a second check: multiple concurrent callers in non-Dev mode that all observe a nil cache (e.g. a burst of requests at server startup, before the first successful load) will each acquire the write lock in turn and each re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json from disk, even though an earlier holder of the lock already populated entryPointAssetsCache. The work is serialized by the exclusive lock, so the first N concurrent requests queue behind each other. After taking entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() at line 48, the function should re-read entryPointAssetsCache and return it immediately if non-nil and cfg.Env != setting.Dev.

findings.title: Exclusive lock is held across file/network I/O on every call in Dev mode
findings.body: In Dev mode the early-return at line 45 never triggers, so every call to GetWebAssets acquires the exclusive lock (line 48) and holds it via defer for the entire duration of reading and JSON-decoding assets-manifest.json (line 60) — and, if the CDN branch is ever enabled, an outbound HTTP request (line 90). Before this change those loads ran concurrently; now all GetWebAssets calls in Dev mode are fully serialized behind one mutex, so a slow or failed manifest read stalls every concurrent caller, including the RLock readers. Computing the result into a local variable and only taking the lock briefly to publish it into entryPointAssetsCache would preserve the race fix without serializing the I/O.
